objects.description: Base metric helper class providing default hooks and vector helpers used by concrete metrics. It is inherited by Angular, DotProduct, Hamming, Minkowski, etc.
Angular (cosine) distance metric with an embedded templated Node layout storing either child indices or a precomputed norm. Provides distance, splitting, and PQ heuristics.

Dot-product metric implemented via angular transformation (Microsoft research trick). Extends Angular and customizes Node with dot_factor, norm, and built flag; overrides distance and preprocess/postprocess.
Hamming distance metric over bit-packed integers. Node stores vector chunks of the bitstring and two children. Provides bit-position split selection and popcount-based distance.
Abstract base for Lp-like metrics that split by affine hyperplanes. Node contains offset a, children, and vector v. Euclidean and Manhattan inherit from this.
Concrete Minkowski metric for L2 distance. Implements distance and hyperplane split creation; normalized distances are square-rooted.
Concrete Minkowski metric for L1 distance, including split creation and distance normalization (identity).
Build policy for single-threaded index construction. Provides no-op locking and a static build dispatcher that calls thread_build once.
32-bit KISS RNG with state x,y,z,c and helpers for coin flips, indexing, and seeding. Used as Random policy for AnnoyIndex.
64-bit KISS RNG variant suitable for large datasets; provides same helpers as 32-bit version.

functions.name: Annoy::set_error_from_errno
functions.signature: inline void Annoy::set_error_from_errno(char **error, const char* msg)
functions.description: Formats an error message using the provided message and current errno, logs it, and if error is non-null allocates and fills a C string with the formatted message. Intended for propagating system call failures to callers.
requirements: If error is non-null, the function allocates memory with malloc; the caller is responsible for freeing *error with free() when done.
msg must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.
Thread-safety of logging depends on stderr and __ERROR_PRINTER_OVERRIDE__ implementation; no internal synchronization is provided.

functions.name: Annoy::set_error_from_string
functions.signature: inline void Annoy::set_error_from_string(char **error, const char* msg)
functions.description: Logs the provided message and, if error is non-null, allocates and copies the message into a newly malloc'd C string for the caller. Useful for returning non-errno errors.
requirements: If error is non-null, the function allocates memory with malloc; the caller must free *error with free().
msg must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: Annoy::remap_memory_and_truncate
functions.signature: inline bool Annoy::remap_memory_and_truncate(void** _ptr, int _fd, size_t old_size, size_t new_size)
functions.description: Resizes a memory-mapped region to new_size, updating *_ptr in-place. On Linux uses mremap plus ftruncate; on other platforms unmaps, ftruncates, then mmaps a new region.
requirements: _ptr must point to a currently valid mmap'd region of size old_size, created from file descriptor _fd.
_fd must be a valid open file descriptor supporting ftruncate and mmap.
old_size and new_size are sizes in bytes; new_size is the target mapping/file size.
On non-Linux platforms, the existing mapping is unmapped before remapping; callers must ensure no other pointers into that region are used concurrently.
Returns false on ftruncate failure; callers should handle failure and not use the possibly changed mapping.

functions.description: Pure virtual API to add a vector item to the index before building. Implementations copy the f-dimensional vector w into storage at id item and may set error on failure.
requirements: Must be called before build() on typical implementations.
item must be a valid identifier within the implementation’s supported range/type S.
w must point to an array of at least f elements of type T (dimension f is defined by the concrete implementation).

functions.signature: virtual bool Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface<S, T, R>::build(int q, int n_threads = -1, char** error = NULL) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual API to build the ANN index with q trees, optionally using n_threads. After build, the index can be queried and/or saved.
requirements: Typically must be called after adding all items and before save()/queries.
q is the number of trees; q == -1 is allowed by some implementations (auto sizing).
n_threads == -1 may select a default thread count; behavior is implementation-defined.
If error is non-null and an error occurs, implementations allocate and set *error; caller must free with free().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface::unbuild
functions.signature: virtual bool Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface<S, T, R>::unbuild(char** error = NULL) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual API to discard built tree structures while keeping items, allowing rebuilding with different parameters.
requirements: Must not be called on a loaded-mmap’d index in some implementations; see concrete class behavior.
If error is non-null and an error occurs, implementations allocate and set *error; caller must free with free().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface::save
functions.signature: virtual bool Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface<S, T, R>::save(const char* filename, bool prefault = false, char** error = NULL) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual API to serialize the built index to a file. prefault may request pre-populating OS page cache when reloading on some systems.
requirements: filename must be a valid writable path for the process.
Index must generally be built before saving; behavior otherwise is implementation-defined.
If error is non-null and an error occurs, implementations allocate and set *error; caller must free with free().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndexInterface::unload

functions.description: Pure virtual API to release resources associated with the index (mappings, file descriptors, heap memory).
requirements: After unload(), the instance is typically reset; further operations may require load() or rebuilding.

requirements: filename must refer to a valid index file built with compatible metric/dimensions for the concrete implementation.
If error is non-null and an error occurs, implementations allocate and set *error; caller must free with free().

functions.signature: Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::~AnnoyIndex()

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::add_item
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::add_item(S item, const T* w, char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Adds a single item vector w to the index at id item. Fails if the index is currently loaded from disk. Initializes metric-specific node fields and updates item count.
requirements: Must not be called after load(); adding to a loaded index is prohibited.
w must point to at least get_f() elements of type T.
item must be within the representable range of S and non-negative.
If error is non-null and an error occurs, *error will be set via set_error_from_string and must be freed by the caller with free().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::on_disk_build
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::on_disk_build(const char* file, char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Prepares the index to build directly on disk by creating/truncating file and memory-mapping an initial region. Subsequent add/build operations will grow the mapping.
requirements: Must be called before building when you intend to build on disk.
file must be a valid path; process must have permission to create/write.
On failure, returns false and sets *error (caller frees with free()).
Not thread-safe; should be called prior to concurrent build phases.

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::build
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::build(int q, int n_threads = -1, char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Builds the forest of trees with q trees (or auto if q == -1 in multithreaded policy), possibly using multiple threads via the ThreadedBuildPolicy. Performs metric-specific preprocess/postprocess. Copies root nodes to the end of storage and finalizes the structure.
requirements: Index must not be in loaded state; building a loaded index is prohibited.
Index must not already be built; multiple builds without unbuild() are prohibited.
q is the number of trees; may be -1 for auto-growth based on items.
n_threads controls parallelism (policy-dependent).
On-disk builds will resize/truncate the mapped file; callers should ensure file system supports it.
On error, returns false and sets *error; caller frees with free().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::unbuild
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::unbuild(char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Discards built tree topology (roots), resets node count to items, and marks the index as not built, allowing a rebuild with new parameters.
requirements: Must not be called on a loaded index; returns false and sets error in that case.
After unbuild, previously saved/loaded structures are not available until build().

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::save
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::save(const char* filename, bool prefault = false, char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Saves the built index to filename. For in-memory builds, writes and then reloads via load() to normalize the memory layout; for on-disk builds, returns true without rewriting.
requirements: Index must be built; otherwise returns false and sets error.
filename must be writable; existing file will be unlinked/overwritten.
On failure of open/write/close, returns false and sets *error (caller frees with free()).

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::reinitialize
functions.signature: void Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::reinitialize()
functions.description: Resets internal state to defaults (clears mappings, counters, flags, roots, and seed). Used by constructor and unload().
requirements: Intended for internal use; calling during concurrent access is unsafe.

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::unload
functions.signature: void Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::unload()
functions.description: Releases resources: closes file descriptors, unmaps mappings, or frees heap memory depending on mode, then reinitializes. Logs if verbose.
requirements: Not thread-safe with concurrent queries/operations; ensure exclusive access.
After unload, the index is reset; further operations require load() or rebuilding.

functions.name: Annoy::AnnoyIndex::load
functions.signature: bool Annoy::AnnoyIndex<S, T, Distance, Random, ThreadedBuildPolicy>::load(const char* filename, bool prefault = false, char** error = NULL)
functions.description: Loads an existing index from filename by memory-mapping it read-only. Validates file size, infers roots from the tail of the file, and marks the index as built/loaded.
requirements: filename must exist and be readable.
File size must be non-zero and a multiple of node size; metric and dimension must match how the index was built.
prefault true may require MAP_POPULATE support; otherwise a warning is logged.
On failure, returns false and sets *error (caller frees with free()).

data_types.description: A generic null-terminated character string with no required format constraints. May contain any bytes except the terminating NUL; suitable for APIs that accept free-form message text.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate a valid null-terminated C-string payload for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers.
# The fuzzers here exercise error formatting/logging paths that benefit from a variety of
# message contents: ASCII, Unicode-ish UTF-8, long/short lengths, percent-format specifiers,
# newlines, NUL-avoidance, etc. We will return bytes that represent a string without embedded
# NULs; the harness will add its own terminator when converting to std::string/c_str().

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '

# Some interesting substrings for error formatting and path-like content
INTERESTING_SNIPPETS: List[str] = [
    "%s", "%d", "%u", "%x", "%p", "%%",  # printf-like tokens
    "errno:", "error:", "warning:", "info:",
    "file not found", "permission denied", "invalid argument", "timeout",
    "C:\\path\\to\\file.txt", "/var/log/syslog", "/tmp/annoy.index",
    "Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3",  # newlines
    "tabs\tseparated\tvalues",  # tabs
    "unicode: café – π – 你好 – 😀",  # UTF-8 multi-byte
    "[DEBUG] [Annoy] building index", "[TRACE] RNG seed=12345",
]

# Some language alphabets to produce UTF-8 variety
UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    "αβγδεζηθικλμνξοπρστυφχψω",  # Greek
    "абвгдеёжзийклмнопрстуфхцчшщьыъэюя",  # Cyrillic
    "こんにちは世界",  # Japanese
    "안녕하세요세계",  # Korean
    "مرحبا بالعالم",  # Arabic
    "हेलोविश्व",  # Devanagari
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII and some unicode blocks
    out = []
    while len(''.join(out)) < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.6:
            out.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1))
        elif choice < 0.9:
            block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
            out.append(rng.choice(block))
        else:
            # Add some control-like escapes represented as actual chars except NUL
            out.append(rng.choice(['\n', '\r', '\t']))
    s = ''.join(out)
    # Trim to requested length
    return s[:n]

def _compose_message(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Start with a base snippet mix
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Decide a theme
    theme = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if theme == 0:
        parts.append("[ERROR] ")
    elif theme == 1:
        parts.append("[WARN] ")
    elif theme == 2:
        parts.append("[INFO] ")
    else:
        parts.append("")

    # Insert some interesting tokens
    k = rng.randint(1, min(5, max(1, target_len // 16)))
    for _ in range(k):
        parts.append(rng.choice(INTERESTING_SNIPPETS))
        # Random separator
        parts.append(rng.choice([" - ", ": ", " | ", ", ", " "]))

    # Fill remaining with random utf8/ascii
    remaining = max(0, target_len - len(''.join(parts)))
    if remaining > 0:
        parts.append(_rand_utf8(rng, remaining))

    s = ''.join(parts)
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; replace if any (shouldn't occur, but be safe)
    s = s.replace('\x00', '?')
    # Limit to target_len
    return s[:target_len]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a length strategy: short, medium, long
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        length = rng.randint(0, 16)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        length = rng.randint(17, 256)
    else:
        length = rng.randint(257, min(2048, MAX_SIZE - 1))

    # Occasionally craft pure ASCII or with heavy format specifiers
    mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        # Pure ASCII printable
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, length)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Include many printf-like tokens
        tokens = ["%s", "%d", "%u", "%x", "%ld", "%f", "%%", "%#x"]
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(tokens + [' ', '-', ':', '|']) for _ in range(max(1, length // 2)))
        s = (s + _rand_ascii(rng, length))[0:length]
    elif mode == 2:
        # Path and errno themed message
        base = rng.choice([
            "open(%s) failed with errno %d: ",
            "ftruncate(%s) -> errno=%d: ",
            "mmap(%p, %u) error %d: ",
            "load file '%s' (size=%u) failed: ",
        ])
        filler = _rand_utf8(rng, max(0, length - len(base)))
        s = (base + filler)[:length]
    else:
        s = _compose_message(rng, length)

    # Ensure no NUL bytes and size under limit
    s = s.replace('\x00', '?')
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    # Constrain to MAX_SIZE bytes
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
    return b
